explanation: In Russia the thumbs-up is used much like in most of Europe and North America, as a casual, friendly sign of approval or 'good job.' A number of generic travel listicles claim it's offensive in Russia by lumping it in with countries like Iran, but Russia-focused sources describe it as an everyday positive gesture with no offensive meaning.
local_tip: Use a thumbs-up freely in casual situations; it will be read as approval, not as an insult.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is a well-documented obscene insult, equivalent to the middle finger.
Thumbs-up can carry a crude meaning in some contexts and is best avoided with strangers.
Some Greeks, especially older generations, associate the gesture with an old sailors' insult, though it's increasingly read as positive among younger people.

sources.title: Russian cultural gestures and body language, realistically explained
